scenes.headline: How a page reader keeps its attention fixed
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pennant! Unlimited OCR two reads very long documents. Here is how it keeps the work per word the same, however many pages came before.

scenes.text: While copying a page, the decoder reads the page it is on and its last 128 words, not every page it has seen.
scenes.say: While it writes out one page, it reads that page, plus its own most recent words. It does not look back over every earlier page.

steps.say: Page Gate drops every block that holds none of the current page's image tokens.
Token Sieve scores the blocks that remain and keeps the best few.
Attention reads those blocks, plus the local window of recent text.
Then it writes the next token, and the read set stays the same size.

items.say: Each block of thirty-two tokens is squeezed into one summary key.
The query is scored against every summary.
A sparse softmax keeps the best blocks.
Their log scores are added to attention, so the loss trains the router.

scenes.title: The advertised budget

parts.say: A hundred and twenty-eight tokens of local window.

parts.note: up to twelve blocks of thirty-two
parts.say: Plus up to twelve remote blocks of thirty-two.
Gives a ceiling of five hundred and twelve.

scenes.say: The shipped settings give a fixed budget.

steps.say: The paper draws it the same way: Page Gate, Token Sieve, and the local window joining before attention.

scenes.label: keys actually read in base mode
scenes.note: a page has only nine or ten candidate blocks
scenes.say: Counting in a small re-implementation, a page has only nine or ten candidate blocks, so a query reads fewer keys than the cap.

scenes.text: The attention work per step is fixed, but the cache and the router's own pass still grow with length.
scenes.say: The attention itself is fixed. The cache, and possibly the router's summary pass, still grow with the document.
Read the current page, keep a short local window, and cap the remote blocks.
